==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|usta}} {{q|informal}}, {{l|en|useta}} {{q|informal}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/juːs(t).tu/|/juːs.tə/|a=UK|nocount=1}}<!--note: the final "u" deliberately has no ː/: symbol after it in IPA and SAMPA-->
* {{IPA|en|/jus(t).tu/|/jus.tə/|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-used_to.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|En-au-used to.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{homophones|en|use to}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːstu|uːstə|s=2}}
* Not homophonous with ''used'' in the sense of "made use of" (as in "the key was used to open the door"), whose pronunciation is {{IPA|en|/juːzd/|nocount=1}}.

===Etymology 1===
From {{m|en|used|}}, past participle of {{m|en|use||{{q|archaic sense}} to be in the habit of}}<ref name=mw/> + {{m|en|to}}.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|-}}

# {{lb|en|idiomatic|with noun phrase}} [[accustomed|Accustomed]] to, tolerant or accepting of.
#: {{ux|en|I am very '''used to''' cleaning up other people’s mess.}}
#: {{ux|en|I became/grew quite '''used to''' his ways.}}
#: {{ux|en|I got '''used to''' this weather.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=5|passage=“Well,” I says, “I cal'late a body could get '''used to''' Tophet if he stayed there long enough.” ¶ She flared up; the least mite of a slam at Doctor Wool was enough to set her going.}}
#* {{RQ:Williams Velveteen Rabbit|passage=He was shivering a little, for he had always been '''used to''' sleeping in a proper bed, and by this time his coat had worn so thin and threadbare from hugging that it was no longer any protection to him.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|year=1965|author=w:Bob Dylan|title=w:Like a Rolling Stone
|passage=Nobody's ever taught you how to live out on the street and now you're gonna have to get '''used to''' it.}}

=====Synonyms=====
* {{l|en|wont}} to
* {{l|en|accustomed}} to

=====Antonyms=====
* {{l|en|unused to}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{m|en|used|}}, past of {{m|en|use||{{q|archaic sense}} to be in the habit of}}<ref name=mw/> + {{m|en|to||infinitive marker}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb|-|-|~|-}}

# {{senseid|en|formerly}} {{lb|en|temporal location}} [[formerly|Formerly]] and habitually or repeatedly, but possibly no longer, did.
#: {{ux|en|You never  '''used to''' like soap operas, did you?}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''used to''' like that band [[long ago]], and I was surprised I still do.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''used to''' know a guy from the UK who pronounced "mother" with the "r".}}
#: {{ux|en|It '''used to''' be me who ran the company.}}
#: {{ux|en|There '''used to''' be open fields here. Now it's a shopping mall.}}
#: {{ux|en|I always  '''used to''' go to the seaside in August as a child.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''used to''' live here, but [[moved away]] last year.}}
#: {{ux|en|The club '''used to''' be frequented by locals; then, after the "incident", it '''used to''' get raided by the cops.}}
#: {{ux|en|My wife '''used''' not '''to''' be so [[hot-tempered]].}}
#: {{ux|en|We don't care about what your dad might've '''used to''' tell you.}}
#* {{RQ:Jefferies Amateur Poacher|chapter=1|passage=They burned the old gun that '''used to''' stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. Otherwise his pelt would not have been so perfect. And why else was he put away up there out of sight?—and so magnificent a brush as he had too.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=I|page=2|passage=He '''used to''' drop into my chambers once in a while to smoke, and was first-rate company. When I gave a dinner there was generally a cover laid for him. I liked the man for his own sake, and even had he promised to turn out a celebrity it would have had no weight with me.}}
#* '''1980''', Björn Ulvaeus, Benny Andersson (lyrics), Agnetha Fältskog (lead vocalist), {{w|ABBA}}, {{nowrap|''{{w|The Winner Takes It All}}''}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1997
|author=w:George Carlin
|title=w:Brain Droppings
|url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780786883219/
|location=[[New York]]

=====Usage notes=====
* With ''did'' as an [[Appendix:Glossary#auxiliary|auxiliary verb]] (as in the negative and interrogative), '''{{m|en|use to}}''' is considered standard in American English (e.g., ''Did you use to walk to school?''; ''He didn't use to behave that way!''; ''It's hard to drive without power steering, did people just use to be stronger?'').<ref name=mw>[https://www.merriam-webster.com/words-at-play/is-it-used-to-or-use-to Merriam-Webster: Is It 'Used To' or 'Use To'?]</ref> In other situations, such as ''I use to go to the fair every year'', it is considered an error to not write the past tense form ''used to'', which is caused by the two forms sounding nearly or exactly the same.<ref name=mw/>
* The negative may be formed as ''used to not'' or ''used not to'' (''[[usen't to]], [[usedn't to]]''), ''did not use to'' (''didn't use to'').<!-- [https://www.adaptingaccents.com/single-post/didnt-used-to https://www.adaptingaccents.com/single-post/didnt-used-to/], [http://www.dailywritingtips.com/addendum-on-used-to-vs-use-to/], [http://virtuallinguist.typepad.com/the_virtual_linguist/2008/10/snowclone-and-bad-grammar-at-clapham-junction-station.html], [http://www.quora.com/Is-use-to-or-used-to-poor-grammar] -->
* The interrogative is constructed like ''did [subject] use to...?'' or ''used [subject] to...?'', varying by region and era.
* The versions ''did not use'''d''' to'' (''didn't use'''d''' to''), or, in questions, ''did [subject] use'''d''' to ...?'' are often seen and may be crowding out the versions with ''use to'', but are nevertheless generally considered non-standard.<ref name=mw/><ref name="RoutlegdeSG">Stewart Clark, Graham Pointon, ''The Routledge Student Guide to English Usage: A guide to academic writing for students'' (2016, Routledge, {{ISBN|9781317391173}}), page 296: "In questions, use ''Did he use to go to Cardiff?'' rather than ''Did he used to go to Cardiff?'' This second version is clearly non-standard. The same applies to negatives: ''He did not use to play football'' is recommended usage, but ''He did not used to play football'' is non-standard. Note that the alternative ''He used not to play football on Sundays'' is correct usage, but too formal for most contexts."</ref>
* When it is not necessary to include the following verb, it is usual in some regions to use the verb {{m|en|do}} as a stand-in (''he works harder than he used to do''), whereas in others it is usual to use no verb at all (''he works harder than he used to'').
* The form {{m|en|usedst to}} is used with {{m|en|thou}}.
